statement: You are given a binary tree. The tree is given as the array tree in level order, indexed from 0: the root is tree[0], and the left and right children of the node at index i are at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2. null marks a position with no node, and every position below a null must be null too.

Give the root column 0; a left child sits one column to the left of its parent (column − 1) and a right child one column to the right (column + 1). Looking down on the tree from above, you see in each column only its highest node (the one closest to the root). If two nodes in a column are equally high, the one met first in a level-order traversal, from the left, is the one seen.
Return the values seen from above, ordered from the leftmost column to the rightmost.

examples.explanation: 5 and 6 also fall in column 0, but they are hidden under the root 1. The other columns hold 4, 2, 3 and 7.
3 is the only child of 7 and has children 1 and 5. 5 is in column 0, below 7, so it is not seen.
